name: Hector Clay
life: “I still remember hanging a new lock after a stranger slept in our shop.” Saturday often includes a stop at the entrance to the Wash House, where Hector stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: He charged me rent for a room he didn't own. I came to the reading because I wanted to hear someone say so.
appearance: Hector is easy to recognize by a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow and a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones. Usually dressed in an unlined tan jacket with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring, Hector raises one eyebrow long before saying yes when listening.
personality: Hector finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To tell the family which tenancy was fraudulent.
family: Peyton Waters is Hector’s stepsibling. Hector remembers the birthdays. Peyton asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The other side of the cove*, Peyton says, “I brought the cleaner a newspaper every summer.”
connections: Ava Nichols. The cook hears from the customer who rented a room the man never owned.

reactions.situation: A late customer's daughter objects to the memorial payment
reactions.response: Hector gives the daughter a private chance to say what is upsetting about the payment.

reactions.situation: A diner goes silent in the middle of a noisy family celebration
reactions.response: Hector asks one close relative to check in privately instead of stopping the party for a public inquiry.

reactions.situation: When somebody waves from across traffic
reactions.response: Hector waits at the corner to hear their voice and give them a proper answer.
